title: PC shipments sank 20% in Q3 as the AI memory shortage hit laptops
key_facts: IDC reported on 8 Oct 2026 that worldwide PC shipments fell to 62.7 million units in Q3 2026, down 20.1% year on year and 9.1% from Q2.
Lenovo shipped 14.9 million (down 22.6%), HP 10.3 million (down 30.9%), Dell 7.6 million (down 25%), ASUS 5.5 million (down 8.6%), Apple 5.9 million (down 11.3%).
IDC pointed to two forces: PC prices high enough to suppress buying, and earlier purchases pulled forward to beat price hikes.
Startup Fortune says memory (DRAM and NAND) is being redirected to AI data centres, raising PC prices.
HP told the SEC on Monday it expects global PC shipments to shrink through 2027 as memory prices surge.
Gartner projects PC prices could rise as much as 17% year over year.
quote_evidence: IDC reported on October 8 that worldwide PC shipments fell to 62.7 million units in the third quarter of 2026, down 20.1% from the same period last year and down 9.1% from the previous quarter.

IDC pointed to two forces compounding each other: PC prices have climbed high enough to suppress buying, and earlier in the year vendors and retailers pulled purchases forward to beat price hikes that were already on the horizon.

Gartner is now projecting PC prices could rise as much as 17% year over year, with the cheapest machines absorbing the worst of it, since there's less room in a $400 laptop's margin to swallow a $50 memory price hike than there is in a $2,000 one.
why_it_matters_hint: PC sales are falling as prices rise, which the outlet ties to AI data centres taking memory chips.
notes: Apple 'smallest decline' claim conflicts with ASUS 8.6%; left out.
